article_title: Embodied learning and teaching approaches in language education: A mixed studies review
citation: Sofia Jusslin, Kaisa Korpinen, Niina Lilja, Rose Martin, Johanna Lehtinen-Schnabel, Eeva Anttila. (2022). Embodied learning and teaching approaches in language education: A mixed studies review. Educational Research Review. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.edurev.2022.100480
title: Two-strand taxonomy of embodied learning in language education: orchestrated embodied teaching versus embodied learning in naturally occurring interactions
description: The review organizes the empirical literature into two strands: "embodied learning through orchestrating embodied language learning and teaching", and "embodied learning in naturally occurring language learning interactions". The first strand covers designed interventions and activities where teachers deliberately orchestrate bodily engagement; the second covers analyses of embodiment arising in ordinary classroom and interactional language use. L1, L2, and FL studies were identified within both strands, making this the review's central organizing axis for RQ1.
requirements: Studies must theoretically use an embodied framework for learning and teaching, not merely mention embodiment
constraints: Taxonomy derived from studies published 1990–2020 in English, Swedish, Finnish, Norwegian, and Danish; signed languages excluded
target_learners: learners across preschool, primary, secondary, higher, adult, and non-formal language education
target_learning_goals: first, second, and foreign language learning and teaching
examples: The review's thematic analysis grouped all 41 studies under these two strands, with different characteristics of embodied learning distinguished within each

article_title: Exploration of domains of educational purpose in K-12 data literacy education research
citation: Fagerlund, J., Palsa, L., & Mertala, P. (2025). Exploration of domains of educational purpose in K-12 data literacy education research. Educational Research Review, 46, Article 100663. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.edurev.2024.100663
title: Two broad approaches to data literacy: disciplinary data-science-anchored versus socio-technical and critical perspectives
description: The review distinguishes two broad approaches to data literacy: one anchored in the disciplinary paradigm of data science, statistics, and informatics, treating literacy instrumentally as a subject-object relationship in which the human learns to master data; and a more socio-technically oriented perspective that accounts for data's pervasive presence and its personal and societal implications. The latter includes "critical data literacy", which the review characterizes as "not a judgmental or negativistic attitude, but a reflective and a questioning approach". The review argues data literacy should build upon other literacies rather than replace them.
requirements: Conceptualizations of data literacy vary in relation to social, technological, and cultural contexts
constraints: The review notes theorization of data literacy is still ongoing
target_learning_goals: Both skill-centric and reflective, self-determination-oriented competencies in data-intensive contexts
examples: The review cites definitions such as an ability to collect, manage, evaluate, and apply data in a critical manner (Ridsdale et al., 2015) for the disciplinary approach

article_title: A Meta-Analysis of Perfectionism and Academic Achievement
citation: Madigan, D. J. (2019). A meta-analysis of perfectionism and academic achievement. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-019-09484-2
title: Two higher-order dimensions of perfectionism: perfectionistic strivings and perfectionistic concerns
description: The article conceptualizes perfectionism as a multidimensional personality trait supported by factor analytic studies into two higher-order dimensions. Perfectionistic strivings "capture personal standards and a self-oriented striving for perfection" while perfectionistic concerns "capture concern over mistakes, feelings of discrepancy between one's expectations and performance, and negative reactions to imperfection." The two dimensions show different and sometimes opposite relationships with outcomes, which is why the meta-analysis analyses them separately.
requirements: Measurement via multidimensional perfectionism scales whose subscales map onto the two higher-order dimensions
constraints: The dimensions overlap substantially (r+ = .32 in this meta-analysis), so their unique relationships require semi-partial correlations
target_learners: school, high school, and college students
target_learning_goals: understanding how perfectionism relates to academic achievement
examples: The meta-analysis coded subscales such as personal standards and self-oriented perfectionism as strivings indicators, and concerns over mistakes, socially prescribed perfectionism, and discrepancy as concerns indicators

article_title: Integrating Motivation and Instruction: Towards a Unified Approach in Educational Psychology
citation: Andrew J. Martin. (2023). Integrating Motivation and Instruction: Towards a Unified Approach in Educational Psychology. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-023-09774-w
title: Two-step integration process: intra-domain then inter-domain unification of motivation and instruction
description: The review articulates a two-step process for unifying fragmented domains in educational psychology. Step 1 involves intra-domain integration, drawing together key concepts within motivation (Step 1a) and within instruction (Step 1b); Step 2 involves inter-domain integration, drawing the unified motivation and instruction frameworks together. The author states that "the joint operation of intra- and inter-domain integration of motivation and instruction holds potential for more coherent theorizing, measurement, and practical application." The process is presented as an illustrative meta-view rather than a definitive framework.
requirements: A unified motivation framework and a unified instruction framework must first be developed before inter-domain integration can proceed
constraints: The review presents the process as tentative and illustrative, emanating from the author's own program of theorizing
target_learning_goals: coherent integration of motivation and instructional theory to support student learning
examples: The Motivation and Engagement Wheel illustrates Step 1a; Load Reduction Instruction illustrates Step 1b; their nexus illustrates Step 2

article_title: A Systematic Review on Students’ Perceptions of Self-Assessment: Usefulness and Factors Influencing Implementation
citation: Zi Yan · Ernesto Panadero · Xiang Wang · Ying Zhan. (2023). A Systematic Review on Students' Perceptions of Self-Assessment: Usefulness and Factors Influencing Implementation. Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-023-09799-1
title: Two-aspect framework of students' perceptions of self-assessment: perceived usefulness and perceived factors influencing implementation
description: The review organises students' perceptions of self-assessment around two key aspects: perceived usefulness of self-assessment, and the factors students perceive as influencing its implementation. Within each aspect it distinguishes individual factors (e.g., age, self-efficacy, psychological safety) from instructional or design factors (e.g., external feedback, instruments, purpose, practice, environmental support). The framework is used to synthesise 44 empirical studies and to guide the design of self-assessment activities. As the review states, it "aimed to synthesise the findings on two key aspects of the students' perceptions of self-assessment: usefulness and factors influencing implementation."
requirements: Empirical studies that present students' perceptions of self-assessment, whether or not perceptions are the central topic
constraints: The review focused on explicit and/or structured self-assessment, excluding implicit self-assessment such as spontaneous self-questioning
target_learning_goals: self-assessment engagement
self-regulated learning
examples: The review coded 44 studies against this framework, reporting usefulness findings for RQ2-RQ3 and implementation factors for RQ4.

article_title: Overcoming Fragmentation in Motivation Science: Why, When, and How Should We Integrate Theories?
citation: Reinhard Pekrun. (2024). Overcoming Fragmentation in Motivation Science: Why, When, and How Should We Integrate Theories? Educational Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10648-024-09846-5
title: Two types of theoretical integration: metatheoretical organizing versus merging constructs and propositions
description: The article distinguishes two meanings of integration. Metatheoretical integration organizes constructs and propositions from different theories in a common conceptual space while keeping them as they are, whereas theoretical integration reduces their number by merging them. The author states that "Metatheoretical integration can be useful as a first step towards such integration, but cannot replace it," and uses the term integration throughout to denote merging that simplifies the conceptual space used to describe, explain, or predict phenomena.
requirements: Theories to be integrated must target the same or related phenomena and show convergence of constructs and propositions
constraints: Metatheoretical integration alone cannot replace merging of constructs and propositions
target_learning_goals: academic motivation
examples: The frameworks in the collection (e.g., Skinner's guideposts and buckets) exemplify metatheoretical organization; reciprocal-effects models exemplify true merging

article_title: Exploring paths of change: Analyzing teachers’ emotion regulation repertoire over time using multi-level latent profile analysis
citation: Hilger, K. J. E., Scheibe, S., Frenzel, A. C., Grund, S., & Keller, M. M. (2025). Exploring paths of change: Analyzing teachers’ emotion regulation repertoire over time using multi-level latent profile analysis. Learning and Instruction, 101, Article 102234. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.learninstruc.2025.102234
title: Twelve-strategy daily-diary emotion regulation measure across two measurement bursts
description: This instrument is the study's measurement design: daily-diary assessments of 12 emotion regulation strategies administered at two time points in a measurement-burst design. The strategies assessed are "acceptance, positive reappraisal, social support, situation modification, situation selection, expressive suppression, experience suppression, distraction, acting-out, self-blame, rumination, substance use". article_title: A study of initial spurt in the case of addition.

title: Two-aspect general intelligence: an abstract (Binet-tapped) and a concrete, mechanical (Picture-Completion-tapped) form
description: The article proposes that general intelligence splits into two forms, drawing on Thorndike's suggestion of abstract, concrete-mechanical, and social intelligence. The author writes that "there is ground for the twofold general grouping," holding that the "Picture Completion test is the concrete and more mechanical form of test" while the Terman Binet taps the abstract form far more. title: Two-stage BDNF account of L-LTP: extracellular tPA/plasmin cleavage at induction, intracellular furin/PC1 cleavage of newly synthesized proBDNF at maintenance
description: The article proposes that TBS-induced L-LTP in hippocampal CA1 comprises two temporally distinct, BDNF-dependent stages: "an induction stage (I) that depends on extracellular cleavage of secreted proBDNF by the tPA/plasmin system, and a maintenance stage (II) in which proBDNF is cleaved intracellularly by FIN/PC1 before its secretion." description: The article organizes its inquiry with the traditional 2×2 achievement goal framework "distinguishing between mastery and performance, and between approach and avoidance". title: Psychological safety competency requires integrating academic training with institutional cultural and structural support
description: The authors conceptualize psychological safety competency as resting on two essential pillars: purely academic and formative actions, and institutional measures fostering cultural patterns and work climates that allow the competencies to be enacted. They argue that "an exclusively academic approach is doomed to failure as, if the health care environment does not allow for the implementation of what has been learned, competence acquisition will only be possible in the cognitive and affective domains but not the psychomotor one." The framework integrates the Bloom-based knowledge, attitudes, and skills (KAS) model with institutional interventions assessed in parallel.
requirements: Institutional environment must permit implementation of learned competencies for psychomotor-domain acquisition
Assessment must cover knowledge, attitudes, and skills plus institutional interventions in parallel
constraints: The authors state no prior instrument or framework explicitly defined psychological safety competencies; this framework is a first proposal
target_learners: health care trainees (residents and students) in clinical internships
target_learning_goals: psychological safety competencies (knowledge, attitudes, and skills for speaking up and supporting colleagues)
examples: The study measured 20 KAS competency items and 9 institutional intervention items in one questionnaire, treating organizational culture and climate as crucial to implementing the competencies

title: Two-hour structured basic-laparoscopy pattern: tasks of increasing difficulty, five repeatable attempts each, learner-to-tutor ratio 2:1, crossover transfer task
description: This pattern structures a brief psychomotor-skills course for surgical novices: after a theoretical and technical introduction, learners perform "tasks of increasing difficulty and complexity" on standard box trainers, with each task consisting of five rapidly repeatable attempts to capture the full learning curve. The design deliberately avoids tasks shared with other surgical techniques to minimize prior-experience bias, and ends with a crossover task on the non-familiar viewing system. The authors designed it "considering a learner-to-tutor ratio of 2:1 and data suggesting the plateauing of learning curves at approximately 10 repetitions".
requirements: A learner-to-tutor ratio of 2:1 with tutors trained in standardized laparoscopy courses
Standard box trainers with repeatable tasks of increasing difficulty
Approximately two hours of training time, given learning-curve plateauing at approximately 10 repetitions
constraints: Tasks were picked to be feasible for novices and to reflect vision and depth perception, limiting transferability into clinical practice
The two-hour format cannot train manually overly challenging tasks
target_learners: Junior surgical residents (PGY-1/PGY-2) without prior laparoscopic experience
target_learning_goals: Basic laparoscopic psychomotor skills such as grasping, transfer and positioning under endoscopic vision
examples: Thirty-eight novices were randomized to 3D or 2D-4 K setups and completed three tasks of five attempts each, with timing and failure documentation by the supervising tutor

title: Two-day induction bootcamp combining ten simulation skills sessions for specialty-transition trainees
description: The bootcamp is a compact induction format delivered over two days at the transition into a new specialty role, here ten 60-minute skills sessions "delivered by either a senior ENT registrar or an ENT consultant". constraints: Artificial mannequins introduce artifacts that impede realism and full transfer of skills to the bedside, per the article's cited literature

target_learning_goals: Technical and non-technical skills for managing common ENT presentations in ward, elective and emergency settings
examples: A two-day bootcamp at St Mary's Hospital, London in October 2022 with ten stations including simulated ward round, NOTSS, airways, SPA ligation, rigid bronchoscopy, cortical mastoidectomy and tracheostomy management

article_title: A Verbal De-escalation Standardized Patient Workshop for Third- and Fourth-Year Medical Students.
citation: Shenai Neeta MD, Fulmer Valerie, Gowl Catherine MFA, See Jordan MD, Peterson Ryan MD, Van Deusen Reed MD. (2024). A Verbal De-escalation Standardized Patient Workshop for Third- and Fourth-Year Medical Students. MedEdPORTAL. https://doi.org/10.15766/mep_2374-8265.11417
title: Two-case standardized patient simulation with contrasting agitation phenotypes
description: The workshop's core component is a pair of simulated SP cases purposefully designed without primary psychiatric diagnoses to emphasize the universality of de-escalation skills. The cases were "intentionally developed each case to have different types of agitation, given that agitation exists on a continuum": an inpatient endocarditis case highlighting explosive anger, and an outpatient case displaying passive-aggressive demands for controlled substances. Each 22-minute case includes reading, a 12-minute interview, SP feedback, and debriefing, run in four simultaneous rooms over approximately 2.5 hours.
requirements: SPs trained in a 4-hour session covering case objectives, portrayal qualities, escalation levels, and case-specific language
Students received a pre-read article and a 20-minute didactic primer on verbal de-escalation techniques
constraints: Each student practiced only one of the two cases while observing the other, a limitation the authors state
target_learners: third- and fourth-year medical students on psychiatry clerkship
target_learning_goals: apply verbal de-escalation techniques to a realistic simulated scenario with an agitated standardized patient
examples: The inpatient case portrayed a patient throwing clothes, using profanity, pacing, and making big gestures; the outpatient case portrayed belittling, poor eye contact, frequent interruptions, and a sense of entitlement

description: The study's assessment element is a two-round simulation protocol: round 1 comprised three consecutive scenarios (a 5-minute baseline scenario, a 45-minute RCDP or PSD training session, and a 5-minute post-test), and round 2 after a 5-6-week washout was a single retention scenario. article_title: Does reading anxiety impact on academic achievement in higher education students?
citation: Soares, S., Boyes, M. E., Parrila, R., & Badcock, N. A. (2023). Does reading anxiety impact on academic achievement in higher education students? Dyslexia, 29(3), 179–198. https://doi.org/10.1002/dys.1738
title: Two-factor structure of adult reading anxiety (social and non-social)
description: The article proposes that reading anxiety in adults is a specific situational subtype of anxiety with two components identified by exploratory factor analysis of the RAT-A: social reading anxiety, concerning reading aloud and others' perceptions of one's reading ability and effort, and non-social reading anxiety, concerning personal expectations of reading ability and its long-term impact on education and employment. The authors report that "both factors were distinct from trait anxiety", and physical symptoms loaded across both factors rather than forming a separate factor. This is the first study to examine reading anxiety in adults.
requirements: Measured with the RAT-A, a 42-item adult adaptation of the RAT-C, administered as self-report
constraints: The three-factor structure proposed for the child version was not confirmed; physical symptoms loaded across both factors
No prior research had validated the RAT-C factor structure
target_learning_goals: reading ability
academic well-being
examples: The EFA of RAT-A responses in the 169-student sample yielded two factors with high internal reliability (α = 0.950 and 0.943)

article_title: The effect of 3D stereopsis and hand-tool alignment on learning effectiveness and skill transfer of a VR-based simulator for dental training.
citation: Kaluschke Maximilian, Yin Myat Su, Haddawy Peter, Suebnukarn Siriwan, Zachmann Gabriel. (2023). The effect of 3D stereopsis and hand-tool alignment on learning effectiveness and skill transfer of a VR-based simulator for dental training. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0291389
title: Two-direction transferability framework for simulator effectiveness (teaching tool vs assessment tool)
description: The article frames simulator quality through two distinct transfer requirements: "To be an effective teaching tool, practice time in the simulator must translate into significant improvement in real-world performance", while as an assessment tool "real-world skill level must translate into simulator performance, without requiring significant time to learn the idiosyncrasies of the simulator". A simulator can satisfy one requirement but not the other, as with early VR dental simulators displaying on 2D monitors. This framing motivates measuring learning gains (simulator-to-real) and assessment suitability (real-to-simulator) separately.
requirements: Practice time in the simulator must translate into real-world performance improvement for teaching effectiveness
Real-world skill must transfer into simulator performance without learning simulator idiosyncrasies for assessment suitability
constraints: The two requirements can be satisfied independently; one does not imply the other
target_learners: Dental students and trainees of high-precision psychomotor procedures
target_learning_goals: Surgical psychomotor skill acquisition and objective skill assessment
examples: The study operationalized the framework by measuring real learning gains via pre/post plastic-teeth scores and assessment suitability via correlation of pre-test score with first-session simulator score

citation: Chen Guoqiao MD, Jin Shengxi MD, Xia Qiming MD, Wang Zhifei MD, Shi Zhaoqi MD, Chen Guojun MD, Hong Yucai MD, Fan Xiaoxiao MD, Lin Hui MD, PhD. (2023). Insight into the history and trends of surgical simulation training in education: a bibliometric analysis. International Journal of Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1097/JS9.0000000000000468
title: Two-stage historical evolution of surgical simulation training: from doubtful usefulness to positive improvement
description: The article organizes the history of surgical simulation training (SBT) into two main stages: "from doubtful usefulness to positive improvement". In the first stage, some held that practical operative experience mattered more than simulator devices; the turning point cited is a 2011 meta-analysis of 609 papers concluding simulation training was better for young surgeons' growth than no intervention. In the second stage, researchers explored novel applications, standard evaluation systems for competency-based education, and stage-specific training programs. The article uses this framework to identify key pioneers at each stage.
requirements: Requires technological development of simulation devices and evidence (such as meta-analytic support) to move from the doubtful stage to acceptance
constraints: The account is a historical narrative drawn from bibliometric and cited literature, not a tested model; the article notes trainees often receive homogeneous rather than tailored training and training validity lacks a uniform assessment standard

surgical nontechnical skills
patient safety
examples: The article cites Dr Scott's three-phase surgical skills curriculum (basic tasks, advanced procedures, and team-based training) as a second-stage innovation, and Professor Konge's work on standard evaluation systems for competency-based surgical education

Simulated hospital setting with standardised written information before each scenario

emergency response skills such as CPR

article_title: Value-added scores show limited stability over time in primary school.
citation: Emslander, Levy, Scherer, Fischbach. (2022). Value-added scores show limited stability over time in primary school. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0279255
title: Two-step value-added model: predict achievement from background, then average residuals per school
description: The article describes VA modeling as a two-step statistical procedure: first, expected achievement is estimated for each student as a function of initial characteristics such as prior achievement and background, typically via linear regression or multilevel models; second, a school's VA score is the mean difference between actual and expected achievement of its students. The authors state that "all gains in achievement that are left are likely to be due to teacher or school effectiveness" once background is controlled. They used a multilevel model with prior mathematics and language achievement, SES, migration status, home language, and sex as covariates.
requirements: A high-quality initial prediction step controlling for relevant student background variables, since everything left after controlling is attributed to the school
constraints: VA scores differ in accuracy depending on the exact model and covariates used; multilevel models outperform linear regression models per the cited literature
target_learning_goals: quantifying school contribution to achievement gains in mathematics and language
examples: The study estimated school VA scores via Level 1 residuals from a multilevel model averaged within each of 151 Luxembourg primary schools

title: Two-dimensional model of social judgement (horizontal warmth, vertical competence) applied to school self-judgement

article_title: The genetic and environmental effects on school grades in late childhood and adolescence.
citation: Eifler Eike Friederike, Starr Alexandra, Riemann Rainer. (2019). The genetic and environmental effects on school grades in late childhood and adolescence. PLoS ONE 14(12): e0225946. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0225946
title: Twin-sibling extension of the classical twin design separating twin-specific from sibling-shared environmental effects
description: The article extends the Classical Twin Design by adding non-twin siblings, enabling decomposition of grade variance into additive genetic (a2), non-additive (d2), twin-shared (ct2), sibling-shared (cs2), and non-shared environmental (e2) components. The article states that "The incorporation of sibling data allows the separation of shared environmental effects into two parts", with ct2 common only to twins and cs2 common to twins and siblings, yielding "more accurate heritability estimates". Variance components were estimated with SEM (AMOS, FIML) on residualized school-report grades.
requirements: School-attending twins of known zygosity plus non-twin siblings, with actual school-report grades rather than self-reported grades
constraints: The design cannot investigate gene-environment interplay; active or reactive gene-environment correlations may overestimate heritability
Non-shared environmental effects are confounded with measurement error
The rather small sample size and wide sibling age range reduce statistical power
target_learners: School students in the numeracy and literacy domains, ages 11 and 17 in the German school system
target_learning_goals: Understanding the etiology of interindividual differences in academic achievement (grades in mathematics, German, and GPA)
examples: A four-group (zygosity by cohort) ACtE model was fitted to grades of 432 MZ and 529 DZ twin pairs and 317 siblings, with cohort and classroom-group differentiation tested via χ2-difference tests

article_title: The Virtual Operative Assistant: An explainable artificial intelligence tool for simulation-based training in surgery and medicine.
citation: Mirchi N, Bissonnette V, Yilmaz R, Ledwos N, Winkler-Schwartz A, Del Maestro RF. (2020). The Virtual Operative Assistant: An explainable artificial intelligence tool for simulation-based training in surgery and medicine. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0229596
title: Two-step mastery-based feedback paradigm with chunked metrics
description: The Virtual Operative Assistant's teaching paradigm follows cognitive load theory by limiting information given at once: metrics are categorized into groups (chunking) and feedback is delivered stepwise. Step 1 covers safety metrics and Step 2 covers instrument movement metrics; the paradigm is iterative, so "the user must achieve full competency in all metrics of Step 1, in order to move on to Step 2", following the mastery learning model. Feedback reinforces positive behaviours and provides automated auditory and video-based instruction for metrics needing improvement.
requirements: Metrics grouped by category; a competency boundary defined against training-data benchmarks; a mechanism to repeat the task until competency is achieved
constraints: Some individual psychomotor metrics may be difficult to teach without special instruction, which the platform addresses with per-metric expert demonstration videos
target_learning_goals: Progressive mastery of safety and instrument-movement components of a complex psychomotor task
examples: Fig 4 shows a trainee receiving classification with class percentages on the first monitor and individualized feedback on two safety metrics on the second, with red/green zones

article_title: Later School Start Time: The Impact of Sleep on Academic Performance and Health in the Adolescent Population.
citation: Alfonsi Valentina, Scarpelli Serena, D'Atri Aurora, Stella Giacomo, De Gennaro Luigi. (2020). Later School Start Time: The Impact of Sleep on Academic Performance and Health in the Adolescent Population. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph17072574
title: Two-process model of sleep regulation plus the Perfect Storm account of adolescent sleep phase delay
description: The review organizes adolescent sleep change within the two-process model proposed by Borbély, "based on the reciprocal interaction between circadian and homeostatic processes of sleep regulation". Circadian rhythms shift toward eveningness in adolescence while homeostatic sleep pressure builds more slowly, producing a biological tendency to sleep and wake later. Carskadon's Perfect Storm model adds that this intrinsic delay "opens the gate" for evening activities (electronics, homework, social engagements) whose light exposure and stimulation further delay sleep, cumulatively producing chronic sleep restriction. Early school start times then force waking against this shifted phase, creating a mismatch and chronic sleep debt.
requirements: The account presumes adolescence-specific circadian phase delay and slower homeostatic pressure build-up; the review also notes extrinsic factors (media use, evening light exposure, homework) are needed to complete the sleep-loss picture.
constraints: The review notes melatonin findings in adolescents are scarce and inconsistent, and that the relation between sleep and functioning domains is often bidirectional, so causality is difficult to establish.
target_learners: adolescents aged 10-24 in middle and high school
target_learning_goals: adequate sleep for health, daytime functioning and academic performance
examples: The review cites Carskadon's transition study showing reduced sleep duration (about 20 min) and increased daytime sleepiness when start time moved from 08:25 to 07:20.

description: The article structures palliative care provision, following Quill and Abernethy, on two levels: I-level so-called generalist palliative care "intended to meet the patient's basic needs for PC in primary care and within hospital wards", involving skills common to all health professionals, and II-level specialist care for more complex physical, psychological, social or spiritual needs. examples: The 4-hour training course taught by II-level PC specialists to hospital health professionals of all departments (I-level), evaluated in this study

citation: Mahler Daniela, Großschedl Jörg, Harms Ute. (2018). Does motivation matter? – The relationship between teachers' self-efficacy and enthusiasm and students' performance. PLoS ONE 13(11): e0207252. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0207252
title: Two-dimensional model of teacher enthusiasm: subject-specific enthusiasm and enthusiasm for teaching the subject
description: The article adopts Kunter and colleagues' conceptualisation of teacher enthusiasm as an affective teacher orientation comprising "the excitement, enjoyment and pleasure associated with both a school-subject and the activity of teaching". It distinguishes subject-specific enthusiasm, a topic-related person-object relation with the subject itself, from enthusiasm for teaching the subject, enjoyment related to the activity of teaching and interaction with students. constraints: The article notes few studies have considered the subject of teacher enthusiasm (subject vs. teaching the subject), so the distinction is rarely operationalised

examples: The study measured subject-specific enthusiasm with three items (e.g., I am enthusiastic about the subject biology) and enthusiasm for teaching the subject with two items (e.g., I teach biology with great enthusiasm)

description: The authors developed a nonverbal communication checklist by reviewing prior instruments and monitoring sample interview videos. It builds on "the checklist of Collins et al. title: Two-path model: educational context relates to learning approaches through a direct path and an indirect path mediated by students' perception of the context
description: A path-analysis model in which the educational context (integration level and teaching format) influences students' deep and surface learning approaches through two routes: a direct path from context to approaches, and an indirect path in which the context shapes students' perception of the educational context (measured with the five DREEM subscales), which in turn shapes approaches. Path analysis with acceptable fit (RMSEA ≤ 0.06, CFI ≥ 0.90) to decompose direct and indirect effects

Self-administered questionnaires and translated scales may limit psychometric properties and interpretation; the lower return rate in LY1 could limit representability of the traditional lecture-based group

target_learning_goals: adoption of deep versus surface approaches to learning

The willingness-to-show-empathic-behaviour items underwent face validity only

perspective taking
compassionate care
